mathlib_searches.query: An exact adjunction induces a derived adjunction whose unit on a single complex agrees with the single of the ordinary unit
mathlib_searches.results: derived_unit, derived'_unit, derivedη, derivedε, derivedη_fac_app and its reassociated form. These give localization-level units and their factorization, but not the exact single-object computation.
No Mathlib hits. Local search found DerivedAdjunctionSingleZero, which treats the degree-zero homology of the bounded-below unit rather than the full unbounded exact comparison.

title: Canonical full derived single-object adjunction unit
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories with chosen unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume the monoidal, tensor, exact countable-colimit and functorial-flat-resolution hypotheses needed for the library total left-derived functor on C, and K-injective resolutions on D. For additive adjoints f:C→D and g:D→C with f exact, X in C, Y in D and c:f(X)→Y, name the morphism X[0]→Rg(Y[0]) given by the unit of the existing full adjunction Lf ⊣ Rg, followed by Rg of the canonical exact single comparison Lf(X[0])→f(X)[0] and c[0]. This is an explicit composite of the existing morphisms and makes no new choice.

proof.text: The expansion theorem derivedSingleUnit_eq unfolds the named cache to exactly its defining full unit composite; reflexivity proves it.
